ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large triangle KLM, with K at the upper left, L at the upper right, and M below. J is located on side KL, P is located on side KM, and H is located on side LM. The line segments JP, JH, and PH are drawn in the figure. The angle 57° is marked at point J, formed by JP and JH; the angle x° is marked at point H, formed by HJ and HL. Then reason: The problem states that JH, JP, and PH are all midlines of triangle KLM. Since JP is the midline connecting the midpoints on KL and KM, JP is parallel to LM. Also because HL is a part of LM, JP is parallel to HL. The line segment JH intersects these two parallel lines JP and HL, therefore the 57° angle formed by JP and JH at point J is equal to the corresponding angle or alternate interior angle formed by HL and HJ at point H. So x = 57.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large triangle KLM with J on KL, P on KM, and H on LM. The image shows the given 57° angle at J between JP and JH, and x° at H between JH and HL. From the text, JH, JP, and PH are midsegments of triangle KLM, so JP is parallel to LM; since HL lies on LM, JP is parallel to HL. Use JH as a transversal cutting the parallel lines JP and HL. The angle between JP and JH equals the corresponding/alternate interior angle between HL and HJ, so x = 57.
